Hi Jordan / team —

A couple of pragmatic recommendations based on the mix you shared:
1) Batching window: for short prompts (avg 120 tokens) set a dynamic batching target around 20–40ms collection window with max batch size 32. This should preserve p99 < 200ms most of the time while capturing batching benefits.
2) KV / prefix caching: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts and user templates; expect 10–18% token cost reduction for the short-prompt slice.
3) Quantization approach: recommend a staged rollout —
   - Step A: Run 4-bit quantization + per-layer calibration on a copy of your largest model; validate on your generation evaluation set (we'll run 2k eval prompts).
   - Step B: If generation quality drops > 2% on your eval metrics, fallback to mixed-precision (8-bit for attention layers) for generation endpoints and 4-bit for rerank/embeddings.
4) Validation gate: Redwood provides a QA pass included in both credits options (one-week run, sample replay). For Enterprise tier we add a custom eval harness and acceptance criteria signoff.

Packaging suggestion (technical):
- Starter: quarterly burst credits + basic caching recommendations (good for PoC).
- Scale: annual committed credits + full Optimize insights and quarterly perf reviews (recommended for predictable unit economics).
- Enterprise: commit + on-prem quant tuning + dedicated perf engineer (for strict SLOs).

Happy to run an end-to-end perf validation using your eval prompts. If you want me to scope the calibration run, send over a secure Drive link with a sample set (or we can use our secure upload).

Cheers,
Soojin
